text:
sara: Heads-up — I'm proposing a small experiment to add a "thaw orchestrator" layer before we un-snooze GPU nodepools. The goal is to serialize drains/wakeups and avoid a thundering herd when multiple AZs warm at once. Thoughts?

junaid: yes please. current scale-up spikes on prod last night looked like 3 AZs racing and we hit COS throttles.

scale-bot: alert: autoscaler surge from 0->60 gpus in eu-west-1 at 2026-03-05T23:12Z (rate 4.2s/node).

maria: what do you mean by "thaw orchestrator"? a controller that gates nodepool activation?

sara: exactly. small coordinator service that hands out ephemeral lock tokens to nodepool controllers. only N concurrent thaws per region, with jittered backoff if you fail to acquire the token.

kevin: model sounds good. we should also ensure a prewarm readiness probe so we don't route traffic to nodes until runtime libs loaded. avoids cold L2 spikes.

junaid: perf note: the autoscaler will still request nodes from cloud; we should rate-limit how many node requests we let through per minute. throttle at orchestration layer, not just kube.

sara: agreement: orchestration layer will: 1) limit concurrent nodepool warmups per region 2) add jittered backoff tokens 3) publish metrics for queued thaws 4) coordinate with cluster-autoscaler via annotation.

maria: any config sketch? I want to see operator annotation usage so we don't touch existing autoscaler config.

sara: plan to use annotation on the nodepool CRD: `infra.redwood.io/thaw-token-holder: true` and the controller will write `infra.redwood.io/thaw-state: acquiring|active|failed`. controllers will respect `thaw-window` TTL.

kevin: pseudo snippet for kube drain gating:
```
# operator runs this after node readiness check
kubectl cordon $NODE
# drain but don't remove from LB until runtime probe passes
kubectl drain $NODE --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --grace-period=120
# mark ready after /runtime-health returns 200
```

junaid: +prom query we can surface: `sum(rate(nodepool_warm_attempts[5m])) by (region)` and `histogram_quantile(0.95, sum(rate(node_warm_latency_bucket[5m])) by (le, region))`

maria: region constraints: eu-central has lower quota and slower provisioning. Default concurrent thaws in eu-central should be 1 per AZ, not per region.

sara: noted. config will be per-region+az override. default = 2 concurrent, eu-central override = 1.

kevin: cost tradeoff: more prewarming -> higher steady cost; but spikes cost us in throttles and SLO misses. we need an SLO cost function in the dashboard to tune.

maria: can we do predictive thawing based on prefix cache hits? e.g., if traffic shows a rising prefix K of requests, pre-acquire tokens 30s earlier.

junaid: yes, we can feed the orchestrator with a simple predictor from infra-metrics. start with rate-of-change threshold to trigger prewarm. Keep it conservative.

scale-bot: info: recommended backoff window = 30s + rand(0..60s) for jitter.

sara: decision: we'll run an A/B on prod in eu-west-1 for 2 weeks: group A nodepools use orchestrator gating (10% of clusters), group B current behavior. success criteria: 30% reduction in simultaneous node requests and <5% increase in steady warm nodes.

maria: can you add a playbook snippet for manual override? we need an emergency "force-thaw" flag for oncall.

sara: yes: `infractl thaw --force nodepool/foo` and operator will honor `infra.redwood.io/force-thaw: true` annotation. will add TTL safety.

kevin: assign: sara to implement controller stub, junaid to hook up metrics and predictor, maria to add region overrides and runbook, me to add runtime readiness gating.

junaid: I'll add Grafana panels and a pager rule for simultaneous_warmups>5 in critical regions.

maria: ping me when the infractl command exists so I can test emergency flows.

sara: I'll spin up a PR draft & design doc tomorrow and link here. thanks all :thumbsup:

kevin: small nit — let's ensure the operator logs token acquisition failures at INFO not WARN for noisy backoffs.

sara: good call. I'll include log levels in the doc.

scale-bot: note: experiment created: thaw-orch-prototype-euw1 assigned to team infra, id=orch-20260305-01.

maria: awesome. I'll schedule a short ops runbook review on Friday.

sara: end of thread — follow-up: PR + playbook by Friday, experiment gating set, monitoring dashboards added.
